title.narrative: UNFPA Women and Girls First, Phase II, 2020-2023
UNFPA Women and Girls First, fas II, 2020-2023

description.narrative:
The Women and Girls First Programme is a joint donor programme managed by UNFPA. The Programme is set up to work for empowerment of the most vulnerable women and girls through pioneering integrated sexual and reproductive health and rights, mental health and psychosocial support as well as gender-based violence response and prevention service.
The Women and Girls First Programme Phase II aims to continuing the work done during the first phase of the programme. The continued focus is to work for people who are furthest behind in conflict affected states, for women, girls and young people to realise their sexual and reproductive health and rights and fulfill their potential through improved gender equality and protection from gender-based violence as well as access to mental health and psycho social support services.

Women and Girls First Programmet är ett givargemensamt program som drivs av UNFPA. Programmets design är unikt och integrerar arbete med sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter, mental hälsa samt arbete mot könsbaserat våld i Myanmars konfliktdrabbade områden.
Programmet syftar till att verka för att de mest utsatta människorna i konfliktdrabbade områden, framförallt kvinnor, flickor och unga kan åtnjuta sina rättigheter genom förbättrat system och service för skydd och tillgång till sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter, mental hälsa och psykosocialt stöd. Fas II av Women and Girls First-programmet bygger vidare på arbetet som påbörjades under den första fasen av programmet.

Women, girls and young people [1] who are the furthest behind [2] in conflict affected states realise their sexual and reproductive health and rights and fulfill their potential through improved gender equality and protection from gender-based violence (GBV) as well as access to mental health and psychosocial support services.
[1] While there are no universally accepted definitions of adolescence and youth, the United Nations understands adolescents to include persons aged 10-19 years and youth as those between 15-24 years for statistical purposes without prejudice to other definitions by Member States. Together, adolescents and youth are referred to as young people, encompassing the ages of 10-24 years. [2] including IDPs, conflict affected people, GBV survivors, LGBTQIA, People Living with HIV, YKAP (young key affected populations), elderly and people with disabilities.
The programme is aimed with the following objectives: 1) Systems are responsive to the needs of women, girls and young people regarding sexual reproductive health and rights (SRHR), the right to safety from violence and safety in emergencies, are adopted and implemented, 2) Improved access to a quality, comprehensive, rights-based package of integrated SRHR, GBV and Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) services 3) Enhanced community resilience and social cohesion towards realisation and and localisation of SRHR, GBV and MHPSS outcomes

sector.narrative: Ending violence against women and girls

description.narrative: The service provision modality for Sexual Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR), as well as Gender Based Violence (GBV) and Mental Health and Psychosocial support (MHPSS) was adapted to the challenges in the context, maintaining or scaling up critical service provision. Following groundwork laid in previous year partnerships were made to expand services, for example through local and community based organisations. Women and Girls Centres, safehouses, health facilities and Youth Friendly Safe Spaces were supported to provide integrated SRHR, GBV and MHPSS services. Total 127 facilities specifically 54 Women and Girls Centers (WGCs), 11 safe houses, 53 health facilities, 6 Youth Centers, 1 Key Population Friendly Space, 2 Paralegal Center and 1 Mobile Delivery Unit (MDU) were supported. The project resulted in over 100,000 persons accessing GBV services, more than 270,000 persons accessing SRHR/basic health services, 138,000 persons accessing MHPSS services and over 660 people accessed SRHR services including primary health care, maternal and newborn health care, safe delivery, and family planning services through MDU. More than 549,000 women, girls, men, and boys were reached through awareness raising interventions, both in person and online due to Covid restrictions. UNFPA established an online platform for MHPSS to support UN staff, partners and community. Peer Support Network is also expanded to support women and girls. The project designed and tested GBV prevention modules and community engagement initiatives like Start, Awareness, Support and Action!
